items.evidence: Vanilla: nextFloat() < 0.5 && nextFloat() < moonBrightness && brightness <= nextInt(8) (two float draws, moon-phase dependent). items.evidence: Vanilla EntityType.Builder.immuneTo is hardcoded blocks: fox -> sweet_berry_bush; polar_bear/snow_golem/stray -> powder_snow; wither/wither_skeleton -> wither_rose. Port immune_tag() maps the same 6 species to tags minecraft:fox_immune_to etc. — none exist in the 1.21.7 jar's data or block-tags.json (194 tags; only dragon_immune/wither_immune, which are explosion tags). is_valid_empty_spawn treats those blocks as dangerous for those species.
items.title: immune_tag tags don't exist in 1.21.7 (fox/polar bear/snow golem/stray/wither/wither skeleton)

Port species.rs:1550 excludes Drowned and its comment claims 'the drowned ... never call it' — wrong. Corrects the 651b43d3 claim. Burn formula itself matches vanilla exactly.

items.evidence: Vanilla EntityType.canSpawnFarFromPlayer is true only for MISC-category types (Builder default: category == MISC) + pillager + shulker (the only two explicit setter calls in EntityType.<clinit>). Port spawns_far_from_player also returns true for all CREATURE types, so creature attempts >128 blocks from the nearest player pass valid_position_for_type where vanilla rejects them. Reachable: candidate chunks need only their CENTRE <128 from a player.
items.title: Creatures spawn too far from players (port allows CREATURE far spawns; vanilla only MISC + pillager + shulker)

items.evidence: Vanilla: y = randomBetweenInclusive(random, minY, getHeight(WORLD_SURFACE)+1) -> [minY, H+1]. Port (spawn_category_for_chunk): y = min + nextInt(H - min + 1) where top = world_surface = vanilla's getHeight value H -> [minY, H]. Port never picks the top value and consumes a different nextInt bound.
items.title: getRandomPosWithin y-range off by one (port never picks H+1; RNG stream diverges)

items.evidence: EnderMan.class contains ZERO occurrences of getWalkTargetValue — Enderman inherits Monster's -cost_from_light (negative in bright light -> spawn rejected). Port maps Enderman to Zero with the comment 'Monster subclasses that override it with 0' — wrong for Enderman (Creaking/Pillager/Warden do override to 0). Narrowly observable (monster spawn rules already require near-darkness).
items.title: Enderman walk-target value wrong (port maps it to Zero; vanilla inherits Monster's -cost_from_light)

items.evidence: 1.21.7 SpawnerData is a plain record (minCount, maxCount) — no IntProvider. Vanilla samples min + nextInt(max+1-min) UNCONDITIONALLY (nextInt(1) still consumes a LegacyRandom draw when min==max). Port sample_count draws nothing for constant entries (26.x count().sample form). Shifts the RNG stream for the rest of every attempt whose entry has min==max (4 of 5 fortress entries; many biome entries).
items.title: Constant-count packs skip an RNG draw (vanilla always draws nextInt, even for min==max)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 EnderMan.teleport grounds on blocksMotion() and LivingEntity.randomTeleport(x,y,z,true) grounds on blocksMotion() too — no tag anywhere; randomTeleport(DDDZ) has no tag parameter. Port mobs/enderman.rs:117 grounds on #entities_can_teleport_to and refuses #enderman_does_not_teleport_to — NEITHER tag exists in the 1.21.7 jar's data or prepared block-tags.json (194 tags); has_tag returns false for missing tags, so teleport_to ALWAYS returns false. All teleport paths funnel through it (random, towards, daylight flee, projectile dodge). Same root cause as Batch 7's B7-G09 (chorus fruit); this is the enderman instance. Secondary: port plays both teleport sounds at the new position; vanilla plays the first at xo/yo/zo (old position).
items.title: Endermen never teleport (grounding uses the absent 26.x tag #entities_can_teleport_to)

items.evidence: tame.rs give_morning_gift grounds the hop on the absent #entities_can_teleport_to (line 1363), so the cat never hops; the gift itself still drops (DropGift is outside the hop gate). items.evidence: Trades::load reads data/minecraft/villager_trade/, tags/villager_trade/, trade_set/; the 1.21.7 jar's data contains ZERO such files and the prepared .local data has no villager_trade/trade_set dirs. In 1.21.7 trades are CODE-defined in VillagerTrades (ItemListing classes: EmeraldForItems, ItemsForEmeralds, EnchantedItemForEmeralds, EnchantBookForEmeralds, TreasureMapForEmeralds, etc.). The port has NO code-path implementation of any of them, and ensure_offers returns Vec::new() when the set is missing — every villager/wandering trader opens with zero offers. Pricing/demand/special-price machinery itself matches vanilla exactly.
items.title: Villagers and wandering traders have NO trades (port implements only the 26.x data-driven trade format)

items.evidence: Vanilla Mob.serverAiStep alternates on (tickCount + id) % 2 (bytecode-verified) and the port mirrors it exactly (ai.rs:2067-2071), so non-every-tick goals tick every OTHER game tick in BOTH, and vanilla goal counters increment per goal-tick — a threshold of N goal-ticks is 2N game ticks in both. The correct conversion is identity. Port goals.rs reduced(ticks)=(ticks+1)/2 halves every threshold/interval for non-every-tick goals (~40 call sites: breed love_time, look times, recalc intervals, bee/fox/enderman/dolphin timers, random 1-in-N rolls). Evidence: LookAtPlayerGoal.start sets lookTime = 40 + nextInt(40) -> 80-160 game ticks in vanilla; port sets reduced(40+nextInt(40)) = 20-40 goal-ticks -> 40-80 game ticks. Breed: 120 game ticks vanilla vs 60 port. adjusted(false, ...) applies the same halving.
items.title: reduced() halves all non-every-tick goal delays — goal-timed behaviours run 2x fast (systemic)

systemic_note: Three systemic threads. (1) 26.x tag/form leakage: B3-G03, B3-G14, B3-G15, B3-G16, B3-G21 and the B3-O01–O06 oracle groups all share one root cause — the 1.21.7 port carries 26.x tag-based logic, data formats, items or APIs for things that do not exist in vanilla 1.21.7, and every such lookup silently degrades (empty tag, empty trade set, nonexistent item). The prepared .local data is faithful to the jar — the port code, not the data, is the 26.x carry-over. Cross-batch: B3-G14/B3-G15 share the root cause with Batch 7's B7-G09 (chorus fruit, same absent tag). (2) Goal-cadence conversion: B3-G17 — reduced() halves thresholds that vanilla counts in goal-ticks, doubling the speed of all non-every-tick goal timers (~40 call sites). (3) RNG-stream divergences: B3-G02, B3-G11, B3-G13 and the finalize draw-order note — values are right but the draw sequence differs from vanilla, so spawn/finalize outcomes diverge run-over-run.
